## 1. Algorithmic targeting: platform credit vs incrementality

The platform serves the top 20% of 400,000 users by a score whose correlation with *baseline* conversion intent is the targeting sharpness. A 50% ghost-ads holdout runs among the users it would serve. Platform credit counts every conversion among served users. 200 replications.

| Targeting sharpness | Served CVR | True incremental per 1k served | Platform-credited / true incremental | Lift-test bias | Lift-test 95% CI coverage |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.00 | 0.0744 | 29.8 | 2.50x | -0.7% | 96.0% |
| 0.50 | 0.1157 | 38.2 | 3.03x | -0.5% | 95.0% |
| 0.80 | 0.1447 | 43.7 | 3.31x | -0.2% | 92.0% |
| 0.95 | 0.1602 | 46.7 | 3.43x | +0.1% | 94.5% |

## 2. Budget transport: a lift test at one budget doesn't price the next dollar

Exact values from a 2,000,000-user reference population. iROAS = incremental conversion value / spend, break-even 1.0. The cost per served user is set to 0.0418 conversions, halfway between the average and marginal uplift at sharpness 0.8. At that sharpness, scaling from 10% to 40% reach is profitable on average and unprofitable at the margin.

| Targeting sharpness | True avg iROAS at 10% reach | True marginal iROAS, 10% to 40% | Marginal / average |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.00 | 0.71 | 0.71 | 1.00 |
| 0.50 | 0.96 | 0.82 | 0.85 |
| 0.80 | 1.10 | 0.90 | 0.81 |
| 0.95 | 1.17 | 0.94 | 0.81 |

Decision at sharpness 0.8: scale reach from 10% to 40%? Each method decides on its point estimate. 100 replications of a 2,000,000-user two-cell test (random halves run each reach level, each with a 50% ghost-ads holdout).

| Evidence used for "scale up?" | Says scale up (truth: don't) |
|---|---:|
| Platform-credited ROAS at 10% reach | 100% |
| Platform-credited marginal ROAS (two-cell) | 100% |
| Lift test at 10% reach (average iROAS) | 94% |
| Lift test at 40% reach (average iROAS) | 1% |
| Two-cell budget-split lift test (marginal iROAS) | 0% |

Two-cell marginal iROAS estimate: mean 0.90 against a true 0.90, with 95% CI coverage 98% (100 replications, 2,000,000 users each).

## 3. Divergent delivery in creative tests

Creatives A and B have identical per-person effects. The platform delivers A to the high-baseline, low-lift segment and B to the low-baseline, high-lift segment (affinity 2.0). Reach is 30%, with 600,000 users per test and 200 replications. A winner requires |z| > 1.96.

| Design | Estimand | A minus B: estimate (truth) | Picks A | Picks B | No winner |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| In-platform A/B, served CVR | Creative effect (truth 0) | +0.0551 (+0.0000) | 100% | 0% | 0% |
| In-platform A/B, per-arm ghost-ads lift | Incrementality of each campaign as delivered | -0.0233 (-0.0232) | 0% | 100% | 0% |
| Audience fixed first, creative randomized | Creative effect (truth 0) | +0.0000 (+0.0000) | 4% | 4% | 93% |

## 4. MMM when the platform paces spend with demand

104 weeks of sales with AR(1) latent demand that the MMM cannot see. Media transforms are known exactly, which is the MMM's best case. The MMM is OLS with Newey-West SEs. The lift test is an 8-week, 20% user-level holdout. The lift-test-as-prior row is a precision-weighted average. Value per sale is 240, so the true ROI is about 0.71. 500 replications per row.
